title: Better Mortgage Turned an Old Email Flow into 30% More Loan Applications with JustAI
summary: Emails matched to each homebuyer's timeline and intent run end to end by JustAI
body_markdown:
Mortgage email has a personalization opportunity most industries never get. A home loan application collects dozens of data points about each customer: whether it's their first home, the city they're shopping in, whether they're after a condo or a beach-house, where they are in the process, etc. The catch is that no two of these people are in the same place at the same time. One is making an offer this weekend. Another won't be ready until next year.


These homebuyers spend time touring houses, talking to other lenders, and going quiet for long stretches. Nothing obligates them to come back. For most of that time, email is the whole relationship. Which puts real weight on small decisions: what message each person gets, when it arrives, and what comes after it. Made by hand, every one of those is a guess you can't check for weeks, and homebuyers don't wait around while you check.


Better Mortgage had two places where it was running old workflows, and both sat on top of revenue.


## How AI-Optimizations were built for both groups


The first group is homebuyers in a very early stage. They have just gotten their pre-approval letter and disappears into house hunting. Some are touring homes this weekend. Some won't be ready until next spring. Plenty are buying for the first time and don't know what the next step even is.


There is also another group in a completely different timeline. These homebuyers already found the house and accepted an offer. All that's left is committing to a rate, and that's where people stop. Largest purchase of their life, rates moving every day, competing lenders calling with offers. Every day of hesitation is a day the deal can die.


Better had the data to tell every one of these homebuyers apart, but not the hours to hand-build a branch for each person's situation.


## Journey one: re-engaging approved homebuyers


Once a homebuyer has a closing date approaching, the job of email changes. Their job is momentum: keep the homebuyer moving toward locking their rate, and keep Better Mortgage top of mind while they do. (A lock is the moment a homebuyer commits to an interest rate, which makes this quiet stretch of email some of the most valuable.) The old flow sent the same seven emails in the same fixed order to everyone, on creative that hadn't been rebuilt since 2023.


The new flow changed two things at once. Better Mortgage's team rebuilt the creative around real homebuyer personas, and JustAI took over how it's personalized: which version each homebuyer sees (first-time homebuyers get a different story), whether they're routed into Better's fast-tracked One Day Mortgage experience, where an eligible homebuyer can get a Commitment Letter within 24 hours of locking their rate, and the piece this case study slows down for: what order the emails arrive in. On three of the seven sends, JustAI is also testing the messaging itself, so the ordering sits on top of content that's improving in its own right.


### The challenge


Seven emails can be arranged in more than five thousand different orders.


Let that sink in, no team can effectively test that by hand. A classic A/B test splits traffic between a few fixed variants, holds everything still, waits weeks for significance, then ships the winner manually, and every homebuyer in a losing arm is spent purely on learning. That's workable for two or three variants. Against five thousand orderings it's hopeless, which is why send order is the lever almost no lifecycle team can test effectively. The order gets set on launch day, and nobody questions it again.


JustAI runs the order as a continuous experiment instead. The machinery underneath is reinforcement learning, a multi-armed bandit that treats every send as a fresh decision, weighing everything homebuyers have clicked so far against what hasn't had its fair shot yet. It starts careful, close to random while it learns, it stays inside rules Better Mortgage set, and it ranks on the outcome Better cares about, a locked rate, and can lean on clicks as an early signal while locks are still trickling in.


The sequence reorders itself as results come in.


### Conversions up 11.2%


The new flow converts 11.2% better than the old one: 14.9% of homebuyers went on to lock their rate, against 13.4% before. During the test period, that came to roughly $28K in incremental revenue over the old flow. The engagement numbers behind it moved the same way. Click rate doubled, from 1.59% to 3.13%. Opens rose more than ten points, from 39.5% to 49.9%. And it happened without an unsubscribe penalty: the unsubscribe rate actually edged down, from 0.82% to 0.57%.


Lock rate up 1.5 points, Clicks doubled, opens up 10.4 points, unsubscribe rate down


When we ranked individual emails across both the old and new flows together, the most personalized new-flow creative came out on top. The clear leader is the email that lands right after approval, the "You did it" celebration: 58.5% opens and an 8.33% click rate, ahead of anything else in either era. The system keeps it near the front because the clicks keep telling it to. It converts too, at 4.07% of recipients going on to secure their rate, by far the highest of any email in the flow. And the sharpest version of it is aimed at first-time buyers: "Your first home is real. Here's how we get you there" drove applications from a third of the sends that its generic counterpart needed to drive none.


The email that lands right after approval. It asks for nothing, and it outperforms everything else in the flow.


### What this means


Send order is probably the most under-tested lever in lifecycle, and not because it doesn't matter. Testing it by hand is infeasible, so it never gets tested at all. If your sequences run more than a handful of steps, hand the ordering to something that can actually explore it. The moment right after someone converts is high-intent and under-used, and at Better Mortgage the email that simply marks the milestone outperformed everything else in either flow.


## Journey two: bringing shopping homebuyers back


The second group are prospective homebuyers who hold a pre-approval letter but haven't found a home yet. Many start with Better Mortgage to see what they can afford. Some then go quiet, either because they're still house-hunting or because they drift away. The journey exists to bring them back to submit a full application once they've found their dream home.


Here the change was the content itself, served through JustAI: nine emails over 21 days in place of eight over 28, each one personalized to where the homebuyer is in their transaction and how they've engaged. The personalization was built on the signals that actually predict movement in this journey.


### 30% more loan applications started


The metric that matters here is conversion: the share of shopping homebuyers who go on to start a full application with Better Mortgage. It rose from 9.25% to 12.08%, a 2.83-point gain, roughly 30%. On about 2,600 homebuyers per arm, that's a result you act on!


The emails were also rebuilt around each homebuyer's actual timeline: shopping in the next three months gets urgency, six months out gets a slower on-ramp. And the strongest signal was the simplest one: homebuyers working with an agent converted at nearly double the rate, everywhere the branch existed (11.43% vs 6.29% on one send). The variants lean into that now. All of it built on data Better Mortgage already had.


### What Better Mortgage's team runs now


Better Mortgage's marketers still own the thinking: the personas, the messaging, what to try next. What they handed off is the part no team can do by hand, matching the version to the homebuyer and re-ranking the send order for every person, every day. Both teams watch the same live view of what's winning, so nobody pulls a weekly report to find out.


The return so far: 30% more loan applications from shoppers, double the clicks from approved homebuyers, and a lock rate climbing behind them.
